mode_plan.rule: Modes do not change the round's state path. council_round declares `spine` identical to its eight states and every registered transition is between adjacent spine states, so a phase-skipping round would require a new off-spine edge, which DEC-052 forbids. Every round that exists therefore traverses the full eight-state spine. `phases_requiring_content` names the phases in which participant content is mandatory, not the states visited; a phase with no required content still occurs. SOLO opens no round at all and so touches no machine.

selection_thresholds.rule: These are defaults, not locked constants: the config-v1 `council` group overrides them through validate_configuration/update_configuration. Selection is computed, never chosen by an agent. `high_risk_classes_default_mode` is a default and not a floor: a user override may lower rigor on any class, because the user is the authority (DEC-013). Such an override is recorded with override_source USER and surfaced, so it is explicit and never silent.

evidence.rule: Grades are computed by the controller over resolved evidence: ASSUMPTION when a load-bearing claim has no resolvable reference, CITED when every evidence reference resolves to an existing repository fact, document or evidence row, VERIFIED when a controller-executed check or spike is stored in the evidence table. An agent-supplied grade is not accepted. Corroboration counts distinct lineage groups derived from static adapter facts, never agent self-report, so Kilo and OpenCode together are one group. A bounded spike runs only through ExecutionService under policy (DEC-024) and is counted against the budget.

reporting.rule: Reports show raw counts with the sample size per agent and per decision class. No percentage is shown below minimum_sample_for_percentage, because a percentage over a handful of decisions reads as a rate. Outcome data is informational only and must not affect routing, thresholds, mode selection or authority.

escalation: After any budget is exhausted the round ends ESCALATED or CAP_REACHED and requires controller or user resolution. The council never accepts a decision because deliberation ran out, and an unreported token count is recorded as UNAVAILABLE rather than estimated.
